model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; residual income equivalent on book, net debt zero)

equity_bridge.item: Surplus CET1 above a 14.5% operating level
equity_bridge.note: CET1 15.4% at 30 Jun 2026 (H1-2026 txt:196) on RWA ~S$278.5bn (31 Mar 2026, Q1-2026 txt:216): (15.4% - 14.5%) x 278.5bn = ~S$2.5bn, ~S$1.51/share. The retention path already funds growth at a 14% CET1; the 0.5pp buffer above that allows for the Basel III output-floor phase-in to 2029. This surplus is what funds the remaining ~S$1.2bn of the buyback and any further specials. OCBC (14.0% fully phased, at target) carries none.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.6% diverges by >30% from revenue (8.5%), net income (9.9%) and EPS (10.4%) 5yr CAGRs, and the 3yr EPS CAGR (0.9%) diverges the other way. Causes: FY2020 is a COVID-trough base (PBT margin 38.5%); the 2022-24 rate cycle lifted NIM to ~2.0% and FY2025 then absorbed S$0.6bn of pre-emptive general allowances (FY2025 NPAT -23%). Book growth is held down by ~50% payouts, the UOB90 special and the S$2bn buyback. Book CAGR is the honest compounding rate for a bank distributing most of its earnings; the base income path (2.5-5%) sits between the two.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF is not defined for a bank; fcf CAGRs are null by design. Periods FY2022->FY2025 (3yr) and FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) from U11.SI_Metrics.csv; shareholders_equity includes ~S$2.75bn perpetual capital securities in both endpoints.

scenario_narratives.base: NIM troughs ~1.70% in 2027 and the drag fades as loan growth (~4-5%) and deposit repricing catch up; wealth and trade fees carry non-interest income, cost-income eases to ~44% and credit costs normalise at ~25bp as the single large Greater China account is worked out. ROE on required equity rebuilds from ~12% to ~12.8% -- still the lowest of the three Singapore banks -- with ~60% distributed. Worth ~1.8x required book plus ~S$1.5/share of surplus CET1.
scenario_narratives.bull: The post-Citi ASEAN franchise and wealth/trade growth re-rate UOB toward its peers: NIM holds ~1.75%, cost-income falls to ~42%, credit costs ~20bp, income +6% for four years and ROE reaches ~14%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Greater China and Hong Kong real estate turns into a full credit cycle (credit costs ~40bp, NPA coverage rebuilt from 42%) while NIM falls to ~1.60% and competition squeezes retail and wholesale income. ROE stalls at ~10.5% and the market re-rates UOB to its 2016-2020 ~1.1x book.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding the regulatory capital its growth consumes, discounted at an SGD cost of equity -- never on statutory operating cash flow, which is deposit and loan movement, and never with deposits or wholesale funding treated as net debt. Profit attributable to ordinary shareholders is the flow; capital retained at g/ROE is the reinvestment; 8.5% is the owner's required return; capital above a 14.5% CET1 is added back as surplus. This is the residual-income answer in FCFE form. UOB is the cheapest of the three Singapore banks for a reason -- the lowest ROE and highest NPL ratio -- and the question is whether ~1.4x book already prices that.
key_risks_to_valuation: NIM: ~68% of income is NII; every 10bp of NIM on ~S$520bn of interest-earning assets is ~S$0.5bn of pre-tax income (~4% of income). July 2026 exit NIM 1.71% is already below the FY2026 guide of 1.75-1.80%.
Greater China / Hong Kong real estate: NPA coverage in the region fell to 42% in 2Q26 and a single large account drove new NPA formation; Greater China is 13% of loans.
Fee momentum: FY2026 fee growth guidance cut to low single digits from high single digits as investment-banking fees softened.
ROE gap: UOB's ROE (FY2025 9.6%, 1Q26 11.5%) is structurally below DBS (~18%) and OCBC (~14%); the base case needs ~12.8% on required equity to be worth ~1.8x required book.
Cost of equity: at 8.0% (the D05.SI rate) the base case rises materially; at 9.0% it falls -- see the sensitivity grid.
Capital: the S$2.5bn surplus-capital add-back assumes CET1 can run at 14.5%; the Basel III output-floor phase-in to 2029 could absorb part of it.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (U11.SI, SGD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 33.25-45.15.
data_sources.financials: U11.SI_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, SGD millions) and kpis table; 2Q26/1H26 news release (U11.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt) for the latest P&L, CET1, NPL and dividend; 1Q26 performance highlights (U11.SI_Quarterly_Q1-2026.txt) for equity, NAV/share, RWA and loans; FY2025 annual report for share capital, perpetual securities, intangibles, diluted EPS and the S$2bn buyback.
data_sources.qualitative: Filings first; U11.SI_Analysis.json for FY2026 guidance (NIM 1.75-1.80%, fee growth cut to low single digits, credit costs 25-30bp, 50% payout) and the DBS/OCBC peer framing.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E recurring total income (net interest income + net fee income + other non-interest income, group basis). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported, so FY0 = FY2026E and year 1 = FY2027. Build: 1H26 actual 7,017 (U11.SI_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:105) less ~200 of non-recurring property divestment gains (Novena Square, Faber House; 2Q26 other non-II +37% QoQ, txt:162-163) = ~6,820 recurring, plus 2H26E ~6,730 (NII ~4,500 with July exit NIM 1.71% vs 1H26 ~1.78%, fees ~1,330, other ~900). FY2025 actual 13,808; FY2024 14,294.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,652.2m ordinary shares ex-treasury at 31 Dec 2025 (U11.SI_Annual_FY2025.txt:8291 note 15) and 1,651.6m at 23 Feb 2026 (txt:12180), less ~4m bought back in 1H26 (cumulative S$794m of the S$2bn programme vs ~32% / ~S$640m at end-2025, at ~S$38), plus ~8.5m dilutive share-plan awards (FY2025 diluted-vs-basic gap 8,561k, txt:8262) = ~1,656m fully diluted, estimated at 30 Jun 2026 (the 1H26 release carries no share count). Held FLAT: share-plan cost (~S$80m/yr) is expensed in the flows, and the remaining ~S$1.2bn of the buyback is a distribution of surplus capital (captured in equity_bridge), not a modelled fall in share count.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. UOB is a MAS-regulated D-SIB: customer deposits (S$426.7bn at 31 Mar 2026), interbank deposits and debts issued (S$44.4bn at 31 Dec 2025) are operating funding whose cost is inside net interest income; cash and central-bank balances (S$35.7bn) are held against that funding (all-currency LCR 159% avg 2Q26). The flow capitalised is FCFE (profit to ordinary holders less capital retained to fund RWA growth) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are FY2025 balance-sheet figures recorded for audit only.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE ~ distributable to ordinary holders = underlying net profit ~5,500 (1H26 2,915 incl. ~170 after-tax divestment gains + 2H26E ~2,750) less AT1 distributions ~100 less capital retained ~1,250 to fund ~3% RWA growth at a 14% CET1 (~S$45bn required ordinary equity). Cross-check: ordinary dividends at 50% payout ~2,800 + buyback ~1,400/yr pace (S$2bn over Feb-2025 to Feb-2028) = ~4,200. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based costs so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes. Informational: the engine projects from base_revenue and the driver paths.
inputs.interest_income_note: Zero: interest income is the bank's operating revenue, not a return on surplus cash.
inputs.sbc_source: Share-based compensation S$80m FY2025, S$83m FY2024 (core_metrics stock_based_comp, cash-flow add-back). Awards settle from treasury shares (2,599k issued FY2025, U11.SI_Annual_FY2025.txt:8320); no net-share-settlement tax line (kpis EquityAwardTaxes = 0).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 share repurchases S$770m (kpis ShareRepurchases; 18.5m cancelled + 3.4m to treasury, Annual FY2025 note 15). S$2bn three-year programme launched Feb 2025, ~40% (S$794m) done by 2Q26.
inputs.dividend_note: FY2025 DPS S$1.56 incl. 50c UOB90 special, ~50% core payout (Annual FY2025 txt:1899); 1H26 interim 88c (~50% payout, H1-2026 txt:23).
inputs.balance_sheet_note: The 1H26 news release (latest filing, 7 Aug 2026) carries the P&L, CET1 15.4%, NPL 1.6% and LCR but no balance sheet; book value, RWA and deposits are from the 1Q26 highlights (31 Mar 2026, U11.SI_Quarterly_Q1-2026.txt:211-247), debt/cash/intangibles from the FY2025 annual (31 Dec 2025).
inputs.book_value_anchor: Shareholders' equity S$52,719m at 31 Mar 2026 incl. perpetual capital securities; NAV per ordinary share S$29.79 (perpetuals excluded, Q1-2026 txt:248) -> ordinary equity ~S$49.0bn. Intangibles S$4,953m (goodwill 4,770) -> tangible NAV ~S$26.8/share. At the current price UOB trades ~1.40x book, ~1.55x tangible book and ~12.6x FY2026E underlying EPS (~S$3.30).
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% SGD cost of equity, single rate across scenarios (scenario risk is carried in the flows, not charged twice in the rate). Built in SGD: 10y SGS ~2.3%, equity risk premium ~5.5%, beta ~1.05 = ~8.1%, +0.4pp for the highest NPL ratio of the three Singapore banks (1.6%) and live Greater China real-estate stress (Greater China NPA coverage 42% in 2Q26, a single large account downgraded). 25bp above O39.SI (8.25%) and 50bp above D05.SI (8.0%) for that reason.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities (S$274m FY2025) are inside total expenses via the cost-income ratio; no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI (S$245m, small) and perpetual capital securities distributions (~S$93-107m/yr) are deducted through cash_tax_rate_path, defined as (tax + NCI + AT1 distributions) / PBT, so the post-tax flow is profit attributable to ordinary shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL: residual income on book, expressed in FCFE form through the component engine, per the dcf-methods routing table row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker' and the house bank precedent (D05.SI, O39.SI, NAB.AX) -- same structure and field mapping as O39.SI so the three Singapore banks are directly comparable. First valuation of U11.SI (no memory entry). Owner-FCF is NOT used: statutory operating cash flow swings with deposits and loans (FY2024 -14,849, FY2016 -13,314, FY2022 +10,104). Engine field mapping: growth_rates = total income growth; ebitda_margin_path = profit before tax (after expenses, allowances, amortisation and share of associates) PLUS share-based costs (0.6%), as % of total income, so the engine's SBC deduction lands exactly on PBT; da_pct_path = 0 (depreciation is inside the cost-income ratio); capex_pct_path = capital retained to fund RWA growth at a 14% CET1 = NPAT margin x g / ROE on required equity; cash_tax_rate_path = (tax + NCI + AT1 distributions)/PBT; wc_capture 0; wacc = cost of equity. Q3 FY2025 (S$443m, S$0.6bn pre-emptive general allowance) is treated as a one-off, not a run rate; FY2025 PBT margin 41.0% is excluded from the margin anchor.

bear.growth_rationale: Rates keep falling and NIM compresses to ~1.60%, trading and investment income reverse, competition for quality clients persists (FY2025 retail and wholesale income both -7%); income falls 3% in FY2027 then recovers to nominal-GDP growth.
bear.margin_rationale: Greater China / Hong Kong CRE credit cycle: credit costs ~40bp (~11% of income) in FY2027 with Greater China NPA coverage at 42% needing rebuild, cost-income ~47% on negative jaws; PBT margin 40.0% (cf. FY2025 41.0%, FY2020 38.5%) recovering to 45.5% (FY2016-17 46.9-47.5%). Plus SBC 0.6%.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin (32.6% rising to 37.1%) x g / ROE on required equity 10.0-10.5% (the FY2015-17 level). FY2027 floored at zero (no capital release assumed when income shrinks).
bear.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.5% / 2.5% = 17.1x terminal FCFE; the 14x cap binds deliberately (~10.5x earnings, ~1.1x required book on a 10.5% ROE), the middle of UOB's 2016-2020 trading range of ~0.9-1.3x book.

base.growth_rationale: Total income. FY2027 +2.5%: NIM troughs ~1.70% (July 2026 exit 1.71%, below the 1.75-1.80% guide) so NII is roughly flat on low-to-mid single digit loan growth, with wealth (+16% 1H26, AUM S$204bn) and trade (+33% trade loans) carrying fees. 5% mid-cycle = ASEAN nominal GDP plus post-Citi cross-sell, tapering to 3.0% by year 10 to match the terminal rate. Same shape as O39.SI, 1pp lower in year 1 for the steeper NIM undershoot.
base.margin_rationale: PBT + SBC (0.6%) on total income. Underlying PBT margin FY2027 ~47.4% = 100 - cost-income ~45.5% (1H26 44.9%, 2Q26 45.3%, FY2025 44.6%) - allowances ~7.4% of income (guided 25-30bp on ~S$355bn loans) - amortisation 0.2% + associates ~0.5%. Recovers to 49.0% PBT by FY2030 as cost-income eases to ~44% on Citi synergies and fee mix. History: FY2017 47.5, FY2018 52.9, FY2019 51.6, FY2021 50.4, FY2022 50.0, FY2023 49.3, FY2024 50.0, 1H26 49.8 (with ~S$200m divestment gains and GA write-backs); FY2025 41.0 excluded (pre-emptive GA).
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at 14% as RWA grows with income = NPAT margin (PBT x 0.815, ~38.6% rising to ~39.9%) x g / ROE on required equity. ROE on required equity 12.0% FY2027 (FY2026E ~S$5.5bn on ~S$45bn = 49bn ordinary equity x 14/15.4), rising to 12.8% by FY2030 with the margin recovery. At 5% growth ~16% of income retained (40% of NPAT, 60% distributed -- matches the 50% payout plus buyback); at 3% terminal growth 9.4% (24% retained).
base.tax_rationale: Leakage = (tax + NCI + AT1 distributions)/PBT. Tax+NCI alone: FY2024 15.5%, FY2025 17.2%, 1H26 16.6% (580/3,495, after the 15% global minimum tax took effect in 2025); AT1 distributions ~S$100m add ~1.7pp. 18.5% flat.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 8.5% CoE and 3.0% growth = 18.7x terminal FCFE, equivalent to (12.8 - 3)/(8.5 - 3) = 1.78x required book at a 12.8% ROE. Cap of 20x is a ceiling only and does not bind.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM stabilises ~1.75% from 2027 as deposit repricing catches up; wealth and trade keep compounding at double digits and the ASEAN-4 retail franchise (8.5m customers) delivers the post-Citi cross-sell; income grows 6% for four years.
bull.margin_rationale: PBT margin 48.5% rising to 51.5% (FY2018-19 levels) as cost-income falls to ~42% on AI productivity and integration synergies and credit costs settle at ~20bp with Greater China resolved. Plus SBC 0.6%.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin (39.5% rising to 42.0%) x g / ROE on required equity rising 12.5% -> 14.0% (still below OCBC's ~13.5-14% and DBS's high teens).
bull.terminal_rationale: Gordon 18.7x terminal FCFE = (14 - 3)/(8.5 - 3) = 2.0x required book; cap 21x does not bind.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 growth default, matching the house bank precedent (D05.SI, O39.SI, NAB.AX). A heavier bear was considered for the live Greater China CRE stress, but UOB already front-loaded S$0.6bn of pre-emptive general allowances in 3Q25 (and has been releasing them in 1H26), NPA coverage is 88% / 306% incl. collateral, and CET1 15.4% is the highest buffer of the three, so the downside is not more likely than the post-Citi upside.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
